3. The present appellants as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.243 of 1984 in the Court of the then 3rd Munsif, Cumilla, which was renumbered as Title suit No. 61 of 1991, initially for declaration for right, title and interest in the suit property but subsequently by amendment of plaint prayed for declaration of right, title and interest in the 1st and 2nd schedules to the plaint and also for a declaration that the disputed 4 registered sale deeds dated 26.08.1975 and 26.10.1978 mentioned in the 3rd schedule to the plaint are illegal, void, collusive, inoperative and also for recovery of possession of the land described in 2nd schedule to the plaint by evicting defendant Nos.6 and 7 contending, inter-alia that the suit property described in the 1st and 2nd schedule to the plaint originally owned and possessed by the Hindu Landlords in their khas who dedicated the same to the Deity Raksha Kali solely for religious purpose and also to bear the cost of Sheba- Puja and maintenance and thereafter, in suit plot No.229 described in the 1St schedule a pucca Mandir with its surrounding walls was constructed and the Goddes Raksha Kali set up and established there-in with due religious ceremonies, pomp and festivities, for more than a century ago; one Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee was appointed as Sebayet of the plaintiff-Deity Raksha Kali and accordingly during C.S. operation the suit land described in the 1st and 2nd Schedule to the plaint correctly recorded-as one debuttar property in the name of the Deity Raksha Kali in C.S. Khatian No.218 bearing Plot No.229/300 and in C.S. Khatian No.600 bearing Plot No.514 as Niskar property; Sebayet of the plaintiff Deity Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee died leaving behin 4 sons Rakhal Chandra Bhattacharjee, Bhupal Chandra Bhattachrjee (uerenaant No.1), Supal Chandra Bhattacharjee (Defendant No.2) and Sishupal Chandra Bhattacharjee (Defendant No.3), being dead his name was struck off from the plaint; after the death of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee his elder son Rakhal Chandra Bhattacharjee was appointed as Sebayet of the Deity Raksha Kali; after the death of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee his legal heirs, above stated 4 sons, are successor-in-interest and they have no saleable interest in the suit property described in the 1st and 2nd schedule which is exclusively owned by the Goddes Raksha Kali and during S.A. operation, under the Sate Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the suit property recorded in S.A. Khatian No.277 and S.A. Khatian No.733 in the name of 4 sons of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee as a Rioti Right instead of the Deity Raksha Kali; Rakhal Chandra Bhattacharjee died leaving behind one son Sankar Chandra Bhattacharjee, defendant No.4; in the 1st part of July, 1984 the plaintiff and the members of the Managing Committee came to know that the defendant No.1 filed Miscellaneous Case No.148 of 1984 in the Court of District Judge Cumilla for appointment of guardian in respect of person and properties of defendant No.4 who was then a minor and said minor defendant No.4 is the son of the Sebayet Rakhal Chandra Bhattacharjee and thereafter, obtaining the certified copy of the C.S. and S.A. Khatian relating to the suit property on 08.07.84 and 09.07.84 and persuing the same, the Managing Committee definitely came to know that the suit property described in the both 1st and 2nd schedule was most illegally and baselessly recorded in the name of the 4 sons of late Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee as a 'rioti right' during S.A. operation. 

 6. The defendant Nos.1-4 in their written statement contended, inter-alia, that the suit property described in the schedules to the plaint is Debuttar property and belonged to the plaintiff-Deity Raksha Kali and they are the Sebayets through their predecessor-Sebayet of the plaintiff Deity and they used to manage all the necessities of the Deity Raksha Kali; there is no Managing Committee for that purpose and for the legal necessities and interest of the plaintiff-Deity Raksha Kali they sold 60 decimals of land out of 170 decimals land from Plot No.514 described in the 2nd schedule to the defendant Nos.6 and 7 by 04 (four) registered kabala deeds described in the 3rd Schedule to the plaint and the said sale proceeds were utilized in repairing of the plaintiff-Deity's Mandir building and making time to time repair and in giving Tog' and distribution of Prasad and for other legal purpose with the knowledge of all worshippers and Hindu inhabitants of the locality who are connected with the Deity for their worship; during S.A. operation the suit property was correctly recorded in the name of 04 sons of deceased Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee, as Sebayet who are the successors-in-interest and at the same time they are the Sebayets of the Deity Raksha Kali; there is nothing wrong in the record made during S.A. operation as stated earlier; the 60 decimals of land out of 170 decimals of land from plot No.514 described in the 2nd schedule to the plaint was sold to the defendant Nos.6 and 7 for the legal necessities of the Deity and it was also known to the present plaintiff and that is why the present plaintiff on 4.6.86 filed an application with verification wherein he prayed to delete the 60 decimals of land which was sold of the defendant Nos. 6 and 7 from plot No. 514 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.600 correspondent to S.A. Khatian No.733 i.e., which is now described in the 2nd schedule to the plaint by the registered kabala deeds described in the 3rd Schedule to the plaint: those deeds are very much genuine and lawful and the sale proceeds were utilized in the interest of the deity as stated earlier and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. Mr. Amit Das Gupta, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellant submits that during C.S. operation the suit land described in the 1st and 2nd schedule to the plaint correctly recorded as one debuttar property in the name of the Deity Raksha Kali in C.S. khatian No. 218 bearing plot No.229/300 and C.S. khatian no.600 bearing plot No.514; one Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee was appointed as Sebayet of the plaintiff- Deity, said Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee died leaving behind 4 sons who had no right and no saleable interest in the suit property which is exclusively owned by the Goddess Raksha Kali but During S.A. operation, under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act,1950, the suit property baselessly and illegally recorded in S.A. Khatian No.277 and S.A. Khatian No.733 in the name of 4 sons of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee as a Rioti right instead of the Deity Raksha Kali and thus, the impugned kabala deeds described in the schedule 3 to the plaint is illegal and void as because the original Sebayet or his successors had no right to transfer any lands of the Deity to any-body without mentioning the name of the Deity as vendor. The learned advocate also submits that as the son of original Sebayet acted as against the interest of the Deity so the secretary of the managing committee being entrusted to protect and recover the property of the Deity, was not barred to institute the suit. 

 14. Having regard to the fact that C.S. record in respect of the suit land was correctly recorded in the name of the Deity Shree Shree Raksha Kali as one debuttar property in C.S. khatian No.218 bearing plot no. 299/300 and in C.S. Khatian no 600 bearing plot no-514 as Niskar property, there after Sebayet of the plaintiff-Deity Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee died leaving behind 4 sons- Rakhal Chandra, Bhupal Chandra, Supal Chandra and Sishupal Chandra. After the death of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee his elder son Rakhal Chandra Bhattcharjee was appointed as Sebayet of the Deity Raksha Kali. Above 4 sons have no saleable interest in the suit property as because the suit land exclusively owned by the Deity Raksha Kali which is immortal. But in the S.A. khatian no 277 and S.A. khatian no 733 the suit property recorded as a Rioti rights in the name of 4 sons of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee instead of the Deity Raksha Kali. After perusing the evidence, of both oral and documentary, we find no reasonable grounds for recording suit land in the S.A. khatian as a Rioti rights in the name of 4 sons of Sebayet Dharmeswar Bhattacharjee. It is a settled principle that the rights of Sebayet are inheritable but the Sebayet or his successors will never have Rioti rights over any debuttar property. The original Sebayet or his successors had no right to transfer any land of the Deity to anybody without mentioning the name of the Deity as vendor and as such the impugned kabala deeds described in the schedule 3 to the plaint are illegal and void. The trial court rightly observed to the effect “সি এস রেকর্ড সম্পত্তি এস.এ রেকর্ডে কোন ভাবেই বিবাদীগণের নাম মালিক হিসাবে রেকর্ডভুক্ত হইতে পারে না।১নং বিাদীর অত্র সাক্ষ্য হইতেই প্রমান পাওয়া যায় সেরায়েতের অত্র কার্যতা নিস্কলুষ ছিল না। বাদী দেবতার নামে নালিশী সম্পত্তি এস.এ. রেকর্ড না হওয়া ভুল।” 

 15. The defendant Nos.1 to 4 sold 60 decimals land of Deity Raksha Kali by 4 deeds dated 26.10.78 and 28.08.75 to the defendant Nos.6 and 7 claiming as the real owner of the suit land on the basis of wrongly recorded S.A. khatian though the real owner is the Goddess Deity Raksha Kali according to C.S. khatian. Upon perusal of those 4 deeds, exhibit 2-2(ga) it is evidence that the suit land is not transferred without mentioning the name of the Deity as vendor rather than transferor (defendant Nos.1-4) named in those deeds as the real owner of the property. In order to protect the interest of the Deity Raksha Kali and recover the property of the Deity, the secretary of the managing committee being entrusted is not barred to file this suit. 

 19. We have already observed that the S.A. khatian was wrongly recorded whereas C.S. khatian is rightly recorded in the name of Deity Raksha Kali. The disputed deeds were executed based on S.A. khatian. Though the right of Sebayet is inheritable but the successors-in-interest that means 4 sons of deceased Sebayets of the Deity Rakhsha Kali can-not sale the property which belonged to Deity without mentioning the name of Deity Raksha kali as a vendor. The defendants also failed to prove legal necessities of the Deity Raksha Kali. Thus, the title on the disputed land cannot be passed by the disputed 4 sale deeds as because the vendors of those sale deeds have no locus standi to transfer the property.
